cards.title: Beware automating SEO before fundamentals work
cards.summary: Automation can amplify broken SEO, so validate fundamentals (technical health, content, conversion) before scaling with workflow tools.
cards.use_when: Deciding whether to invest in SEO automation tooling for an online store.

cards.title: Add a CTA to meta descriptions and differentiate from competitors in the SERP
cards.summary: Improve click-through from search results by adding a within-limit call to action and standing out from competing snippets, a lever before rankings improve.
cards.use_when: Ecommerce SEO where pages rank but get few clicks, or while waiting for ranking gains and wanting more clicks from current positions.

cards.title: Automate Instagram media to Google Business Profile
cards.summary: Trigger a no-code workflow so every Instagram business post is auto-published as Google Business Profile media, building local SEO signals without manual uploads.
cards.use_when: You manage a local store with an Instagram business account and a Google Business Profile, and want to keep local listings fresh without manually re-uploading images or videos.

cards.title: Auto-convert blog posts into Google Business posts via RSS
cards.summary: Use an RSS-feed trigger plus an internet-enabled LLM to rewrite each new blog post into a sub-1,500-character Google Business post with a CTA link.
cards.use_when: You publish blog content and want an automated, ongoing stream of Google Business posts driving traffic back to those articles without manual rewriting.

cards.title: Auto-respond to positive Google reviews, gate negative ones
cards.summary: Filter reviews by star rating and let an LLM draft and post replies only to positive reviews, keeping negative ones for human handling.
cards.use_when: You want to maintain fast, consistent responses to positive local reviews at scale while keeping full human control over reputation-sensitive negative feedback.

cards.title: Choose an automation platform by skill and scale
cards.summary: Match the no-code/self-host automation tool to your coding comfort and volume: Pabbly for lowest friction, Make for flexibility, n8n for scale and cost savings.
cards.use_when: You are deciding which automation tool to run your store's SEO/marketing workflows on, weighing ease of setup against cost and flexibility.

cards.title: Use one Open Router key to test and route LLM models
cards.summary: Adopt a single Open Router API key to access many LLMs, test model quality on a simple prompt, and route cheap models for high-volume automations.
cards.use_when: You need to pick and pay for LLMs for store automations (content rewriting, review replies) without managing multiple provider accounts or API keys.

cards.title: Don't automate SEO before the fundamentals work
cards.summary: Resist automating everything at scale until your core SEO is sound, because premature automation causes costly 'horror case' failures.
cards.use_when: You are tempted to automate listing posts, review replies or content repurposing before your store's SEO basics (site structure, content quality, local profile setup) are in good shape.

cards.title: Skip heavy dashboards: GSC + GA into an LLM for decisions
cards.summary: Use Google Search Console and Google Analytics data fed to an LLM instead of building elaborate reports, so you still make data-driven decisions quickly.
cards.use_when: You need recurring store SEO decisions (which pages/queries/locations to prioritize) but lack time or budget for polished reporting dashboards.

cards.title: Diagnose why your Shopify SEO has failed (short-term game, one keyword, too many)
cards.summary: Four recurring failure patterns behind ecommerce SEO — short-term expectations, single-keyword bets, targeting everything, expecting a silver bullet — and how to reframe SEO as a monthly maintenance cycle.
cards.use_when: You have a live Shopify store and previous organic search efforts have produced flat or declining sales, and you need to decide whether to keep investing or restructure your approach.

cards.title: How search works: relevance signals plus backlink authority
cards.summary: Google matches a query against pages in its index for relevance, then weighs off-page authority via backlinks — which is why a lower-relevance page with a high-authority link can outrank better-optimized pages.
cards.use_when: You are deciding where to spend effort on a Shopify collection or product page — on-page optimization, link acquisition, or both — and need a mental model of how rankings are actually decided.

cards.title: Validate keywords with the C + Volume + KD + CPC filter before writing anything
cards.summary: Screen candidate keywords for commercial intent, volume over 1,000, keyword difficulty below 40, and CPC above $1 in Semrush before committing content or page work.
cards.use_when: You are choosing which product or collection keywords to target on your store this month and need a go/no-go filter instead of guessing.

cards.title: Build keyword clusters around a hero keyword instead of stuffing one term
cards.summary: Because Google now evaluates whole-page context, replace single-keyword targeting with a hero keyword supported by clusters of related commercial terms across the same page.
cards.use_when: You are planning a collection page or blog structure and deciding which keywords belong on the same page versus separate pages.

cards.title: Set up Semrush with a free plan and position tracking for your store
cards.summary: Register a limited free Semrush account and use Projects + Position Tracking to receive weekly ranking updates for 3–5 validated keywords.
cards.use_when: You want ongoing visibility of keyword rankings for your Shopify store without paying for a full SEO suite yet.

cards.title: Run the monthly SEO cycle as a recurring operating rhythm
cards.summary: Execute a repeating four-stage cycle — keywords, page updates, content, links — every month on a fixed calendar day.
cards.use_when: You need a repeatable monthly operating cadence for organic search on your store rather than ad-hoc one-off optimization.

cards.title: Optimize collection pages first, not individual product pages
cards.summary: Target commercial keywords with collection pages first because they aggregate products, build topical relevance across a cluster, and signal that you are a real store with range.
cards.use_when: You are deciding whether to spend SEO effort on a product page or a category/collection page for a keyword like 'natural soap'.

cards.title: Write Shopify meta titles/descriptions for clicks, not just rankings
cards.summary: Treat the Shopify Search Engine Listing as a CTR asset: include the keyword but add a purchase-oriented CTA and beat competitor listings.
cards.use_when: You are filling in the meta title and description fields on a Shopify collection or product page and want more clicks from existing rankings.

cards.title: Feed the search engine monthly with cheap, repeatable content updates
cards.summary: Publish something tied to the month's keyword theme using whatever content type your store can sustain — products, reviews, collections, support articles, or blogs.
cards.use_when: You need an ongoing content cadence for SEO but can't always add products, get new reviews, or create new collections.

cards.title: Use persona-rich ChatGPT prompts to draft SEO blog content
cards.summary: Give ChatGPT an author persona, an audience persona, chosen keywords, language and tone before asking for titles, then the article, then a photo brief.
cards.use_when: You are producing a blog post for a month's keyword cluster on your store and want non-generic copy rather than a one-line prompt result.

cards.title: Rewrite the last 10–20% of AI drafts and run a detector before publishing
cards.summary: AI-generated blog content must be checked with an AI detector and manually rewritten so Google does not ignore or devalue it.
cards.use_when: You are about to publish an AI-drafted blog post, collection description or other SEO content on your store.

cards.title: Keep an SEO content log and monthly tracker to close the loop
cards.summary: Track which keywords you've targeted, which pages and blogs you've published, and how rankings move, so each monthly cycle builds on the last.
cards.use_when: You are running the monthly SEO cycle and need to decide whether to reinforce a keyword, change page copy, or move to a new cluster.

cards.title: Monthly SEO Keyword Evaluation Cycle
cards.summary: Run a recurring monthly review of your target keywords to confirm they are still worth ranking for, and swap them out when they are not.
cards.use_when: Planning the SEO work cadence for your store, or setting up a standing process to decide which categories, collections or blog topics to optimize next.

cards.title: Pick One Category and Build a 90-Day Domination Quarter
cards.summary: Focus all search and content work on a single product category for one quarter instead of spreading across the whole catalog.
cards.use_when: Planning the quarterly SEO/AEO roadmap for a store with many categories, deciding which category to attack first.

cards.title: Map Category Content to the Five Stages of Customer Awareness
cards.summary: Build the category content plan by listing topics at each awareness stage, starting from bottom-funnel most-aware queries.
cards.use_when: Turning a chosen product category into an organized content plan for blog, PDPs and landing pages.

cards.title: Extract AI Citations and Blend Them with Traditional SERP Data
cards.summary: For each core query, export AI citations and traditional search results into one sheet to see which domains you must earn coverage on.
cards.use_when: Prioritizing off-site outreach, sponsored posts and partnerships for a category campaign.

cards.title: Earn Coverage on the Most-Cited Retrieval Domains
cards.summary: Target the third-party pages AI systems actually cite for your category and pursue inclusion, sponsorship or partnership.
cards.use_when: Planning off-site placements for a category where your brand does not yet appear in AI answers.

cards.title: Attack Competitor Comparison, Review and Alternatives Queries
cards.summary: Build pages for competitor reviews, alternatives, head-to-head and '[competitor] vs [you]' queries to capture high-intent category demand.
cards.use_when: Creating content that intercepts shoppers comparing brands before purchase in your category.

cards.title: Repeat the Same Category Queries Across Every Owned Channel
cards.summary: Publish the same core category topics on website, YouTube, LinkedIn, Instagram and TikTok to build multi-surface topic authority.
cards.use_when: Deciding where to distribute category content beyond the store blog and PDPs.

cards.title: Use LinkedIn as a Parasite SEO Surface for Category Queries
cards.summary: Publish category articles on the LinkedIn company page and amplify with employee shares to rank on the strength of LinkedIn's domain authority.
cards.use_when: Trying to appear in traditional search results for a category query without waiting for your own domain to rank.

cards.title: Prioritize Reddit Threads Already Appearing in Retrieval
cards.summary: Target Reddit threads that AI systems already cite, then monitor subreddits daily for new opportunities.
cards.use_when: Getting brand or product mentions into community threads that influence purchase decisions in your category.

cards.title: Build Owned Marketplace Presence Where AI Retrieval Cites It
cards.summary: If a major marketplace is cited for your category, sell or list there to capture that retrieval surface.
cards.use_when: Deciding whether to extend a category onto marketplaces like Amazon.

cards.title: Understand Retrieval Mechanics: Static Corpus First, Then Web
cards.summary: AI answers use model training data first and then web retrieval for grounding, which is why third-party citations influence recommendations.
cards.use_when: Explaining to stakeholders why AI answers mention certain brands, and deciding whether to optimize content for retrieval.

cards.title: Model Query Fan-Out by Repeating Brand Coverage Across Variants
cards.summary: AI runs many related sub-queries after a search; repeated brand presence across those variants is what influences recommendations.
cards.use_when: Deciding how many assets and intents to cover for one category.

cards.title: Ground AI Strategy Prompts in Your Real Pages and Performance Data
cards.summary: Feed the model your category and product pages — and performance data where available — so its strategy output reflects reality rather than generic model knowledge.
cards.use_when: Generating a category content strategy or hub plan with an AI assistant.

cards.title: Run Quick Topic Coverage and Intent-Variant Checks Without Tools
cards.summary: Use plain search and a small keyword tracker sample to measure how much category coverage you already have.
cards.use_when: Sizing an existing category cluster before planning content investment.

cards.title: Reverse-Engineer Single-Focus Competitors and Consider Micro-Brand Angles
cards.summary: Study competitors who only do your category, and consider whether a dedicated sub-brand/domain could win that relevance.
cards.use_when: Assessing how hard a category niche is to win and whether to launch a niche brand or site.

cards.title: Refresh the Opportunity Blend and Flag Outreach Targets
cards.summary: Maintain a single deduplicated sheet of traditional and AI sources per query, flagging repeat domains as the outreach shortlist.
cards.use_when: Managing the ongoing off-site priority list for a category campaign.

cards.title: Budget Time and Resourcing for Category Domination Realistically
cards.summary: Category domination is a high-volume, multi-surface effort requiring hours of content production before moving to the next category.
cards.use_when: Setting expectations and resourcing for a category-focused search program.

cards.title: Diagnose Which Off-Site Channels Own Your Category Queries
cards.summary: Map the recurring top-10 domains (marketplaces, publishers, review sites, forums) across a category's head queries to find the channels worth attacking.
cards.use_when: Planning which channels to invest in (Amazon, third-party review content, earned placements) for a product category you want to rank in.

cards.title: Choose Blog vs Category Page for a Long-Tail Commercial Query
cards.summary: Before building content for a niche query, search your own site to decide whether a new category page would duplicate an existing one.
cards.use_when: Deciding where to publish content targeting a modifier query such as 'best creatine for vegans' or 'creatine for sensitive stomachs'.

cards.title: Brief an AI Listicle with Your Brand Placed First
cards.summary: Ground an AI-generated comparison listicle by specifying your product as the number-one recommendation and feeding it real differentiators.
cards.use_when: Producing 'best X for Y' listicle content where you want your product to be the top pick.

cards.title: Mine AI-Built Briefs for Entities, Questions and Gaps
cards.summary: Use the generated brief to capture competitor-derived entities, People Also Ask questions and coverage gaps before writing.
cards.use_when: Reviewing a content brief before drafting a comparison or category-support article.

cards.title: Treat AI Drafts as First Drafts: Fact-Check and Restructure
cards.summary: AI listicles need explicit numbers, verified facts and tighter formatting before production.
cards.use_when: Reviewing a generated product comparison draft before publishing to a PDP-adjacent or blog asset.

cards.title: Run a Page-Level Audit for Both Search and AI Retrieval
cards.summary: Audit an existing category or product page across crawl, content, structure, freshness, performance and agent-readiness before optimising.
cards.use_when: Improving an underperforming category page or product page so it ranks in traditional search and is usable as an AI retrieval source.

cards.title: Get Indexed by CCBot to Be Baked Into AI Training
cards.summary: Ensure Common Crawl's crawler can access your store so your pages can enter the datasets used to train language models.
cards.use_when: Setting crawl policy, robots rules or bot access for an ecommerce site that wants long-term AI visibility.

cards.title: Optimise for Agent Navigation, Not Just Human Design
cards.summary: Make your storefront machine-navigable because a growing share of queries are resolved by bots that deconstruct your code.
cards.use_when: Prioritising a technical roadmap for a store where AI assistants and crawlers may be the first visitor to a product or category page.

cards.title: Build a Hub-and-Spoke Content System Around the Category Page
cards.summary: Publish modifier-query assets that all link back to a central category page to concentrate authority.
cards.use_when: Structuring content coverage for a product line where multiple niche variants drive searches.

cards.title: Reframe Search Strategy as Full Digital Marketing
cards.summary: Search visibility now depends on on-site quality plus off-site presence, so budget both, not just SEO tactics.
cards.use_when: Allocating budget and headcount between on-site content and off-site earned/marketplace work for a store's search programme.

cards.title: Use Benchmark and Competitor Reports to Scope a Category
cards.summary: Establish current visibility benchmarks and identify top competitors before deciding what content to build.
cards.use_when: Kicking off a search programme for a new product category and needing a baseline.

cards.title: Adapt the Found–Matched–Chosen framework to AI search
cards.summary: Map three checkpoints — discoverability, factual query matching, and external reputation — onto a Shopify store's AI search readiness.
cards.use_when: Planning an AI search / GEO roadmap for a Shopify store and deciding which stage to fix first.

cards.title: Check whether AI crawlers can actually access your store
cards.summary: Verify robots.txt and run a crawler-style fetch to confirm AI agents can reach your Shopify pages.
cards.use_when: Auditing a Shopify store's crawlability before any AI search content work, or diagnosing why an AI tool can't describe a product.

cards.title: See your product page the way a JS-blind crawler sees it
cards.summary: Compare initial HTML with rendered product content to identify crawler-dependent visibility gaps.
cards.use_when: Diagnosing whether reviews, FAQs or spec content on a Shopify product page is invisible to AI crawlers.

cards.title: Publish factual product attributes for specific shopper queries
cards.summary: Help search systems match products to explicit customer requirements.
cards.use_when: Improving ecommerce product discoverability and accurate product matching in search.

cards.title: Audit Shopify catalog readiness alongside storefront SEO
cards.summary: Treat backend catalog data and storefront crawlability as separate distribution checks.
cards.use_when: Improving ecommerce product discoverability and accurate product matching in search.

cards.title: Validate product structured data against visible store facts
cards.summary: Make product facts machine-readable without inventing schema claims.
cards.use_when: Improving ecommerce product discoverability and accurate product matching in search.

cards.title: Set Up a Domain Property in Google Search Console
cards.summary: Choose the Domain property type and complete DNS verification so no URL variant of the store slips through tracking.
cards.use_when: Starting organic search measurement for a store, or migrating from an old URL-prefix property that only covers one subdomain or protocol.

cards.title: Read Overall Search Performance With Compare Mode
cards.summary: Use clicks, impressions, CTR, and average position with a period comparison to answer high-level growth questions on one screen.
cards.use_when: Monthly or quarterly reporting on organic traffic to the store, or when deciding whether a decline needs investigation.

cards.title: Isolate Non-Branded Clicks With Custom Regex
cards.summary: Filter out branded queries using a doesn't-match regex so reports show only traffic from people who did not already know the brand.
cards.use_when: Proving content or SEO impact to leadership, or setting traffic goals where branded demand would flatter the numbers.

cards.title: Diagnose Indexation Status With URL Inspection
cards.summary: Tell apart 'discovered - currently not indexed' and 'crawled - currently not indexed' to decide whether a page needs links, better content, or patience.
cards.use_when: A product, category, or landing page is published but not appearing in Google results.

cards.title: Audit Site-Level Not-Indexed Pages by Reason
cards.summary: Review the Pages report grouped by exclusion reason and confirm each exclusion is deliberate rather than an accident.
cards.use_when: Technical health audits, pre- or post-launch checks, or when organic traffic to key store pages is unexpectedly missing.

cards.title: Track a Specific Page or Keyword Without a Paid Rank Tracker
cards.summary: Use page and exact-query filters plus compare mode to turn Search Console into a free rank tracker for money pages and target keywords.
cards.use_when: Monitoring ranking movement on a cornerstone product page, category, or a cluster of posts over time.

cards.title: Find the Pages Behind a Traffic Drop
cards.summary: Sort the comparison table by click difference ascending to surface the exact URLs that lost traffic and look for patterns across them.
cards.use_when: Organic traffic fell and the cause is unclear, especially after an algorithm update.

cards.title: Re-Target a Page Using Its Own Query Data
cards.summary: Check which queries already generate clicks for a page and align the title and H1 to the query Google is actually rewarding.
cards.use_when: Post-publish optimization of a product page, category, or blog post that targets a keyword in its title tag.

cards.title: Mine Question Queries for FAQ and Content Ideas
cards.summary: Regex-filter question-word queries to find real questions the site already surfaces for, then build direct answers.
cards.use_when: Planning FAQ sections, support content, or new pages that should answer buyer questions explicitly.

cards.title: Get Backlink and Internal Link Data Free From Search Console
cards.summary: Use the Links report for most-linked pages, internal link counts, and referring sites, then route authority toward pages you want to rank.
cards.use_when: Planning internal linking during a product launch or category push, or auditing which pages carry authority.

cards.title: Fix Video Indexing by Building Dedicated Watch Pages
cards.summary: Give important videos their own page where the video is the main event so Google indexes the video, not just the page.
cards.use_when: Publishing product demos, tutorials, or reviews that should earn video results and thumbnails.

cards.title: Use the Discover and Google News Reports for Non-Query Traffic
cards.summary: Read feeds-driven traffic separately, because Discover and News show pages and impressions rather than queries.
cards.use_when: Checking whether visual, timely, or list-driven store content earns traffic outside classic search.

cards.title: Diagnose Falling Clicks With Stable Rankings
cards.summary: When positions hold but clicks shrink, check CTR against position to decide between a snippet refresh and an AI-overview answer stealing the click.
cards.use_when: Organic clicks decline while rank tracking shows no meaningful position loss.

cards.title: Read the Generative AI Performance Report for AEO Benchmarks
cards.summary: Use Google's AI visibility report to see impressions inside AI Overviews and AI mode, broken down by page, country, and device.
cards.use_when: Assessing how much of your content is being consumed in AI answers, or deciding whether to opt out of AI features.

cards.title: Build a Content Plan From Exported Query Data
cards.summary: Export queries, compare them against your sitemap, and ask an LLM where coverage gaps exist.
cards.use_when: The content calendar is empty and you need new product-page, category, or blog topics grounded in real search demand.

cards.title: Track Rankings Automatically and Flag Refresh Candidates
cards.summary: Set up monitoring that flags pages slipping to positions 6-8 and pages whose rankings drop over a 7-day stretch.
cards.use_when: Managing a large content library where manually filtering Search Console for every page is impractical.

cards.title: Split Branded From Non-Branded in Ongoing Reporting
cards.summary: Keep branded search visible as its own metric while excluding it from earned-traffic reporting.
cards.use_when: Building a recurring organic dashboard or content KPI set for a store.

cards.title: Add Social Accounts as Search Console Properties
cards.summary: Use platform properties to see which search terms lead people to social posts, even for an account with no website attached.
cards.use_when: Attributing search-driven discovery to Instagram, TikTok, X, or YouTube content that feeds the store funnel.

cards.title: Map AI Visibility Beyond Google With a Brand Tracker
cards.summary: Supplement Google's AI report by tracking brand mentions and citations across major AI models.
cards.use_when: AEO reporting where you need to know whether you are recommended, how you are described, and which sources models cite.

cards.title: Prioritize a shortlist of business-driving keywords instead of ranking for everything
cards.summary: Start SEO planning by naming the handful of keywords that actually represent buyers, then accept you can't and shouldn't own the whole keyword universe.
cards.use_when: Keyword roadmap planning for an online store — deciding which product, category and service terms deserve page builds this quarter.

cards.title: Run the SERP intent check before writing any page
cards.summary: Google your target keyword first and let the format of the top results tell you what page type Google assumes the searcher wants.
cards.use_when: Before building or rewriting a PDP, category page, homepage or landing page for a target keyword.

cards.title: Use the roundup post backdoor when you can't outrank enterprise homepages
cards.summary: Publish an objective 'best of' comparison that includes competitors so a lower-authority store can rank for a competitive commercial keyword.
cards.use_when: Merchandising or content decision when a high-value category keyword is owned by big-brand homepages and your domain lacks their authority.

cards.title: Match the SERP's format, then differentiate on substance not word count
cards.summary: Build each money page in the format Google already rewards for that keyword, and compete by covering the topic more completely instead of writing longer.
cards.use_when: Building or rewriting a PDP, category page or landing page after the SERP intent check.

cards.title: Prove first-hand experience on money pages and supporting content
cards.summary: Google's E-E-A-T evaluation rewards visible evidence that you actually used or did the thing, with Experience weighted heavily per the source.
cards.use_when: Auditing or upgrading product pages, buying guides and comparison content so they look earned rather than assembled.

cards.title: Build topical authority clusters around each money page
cards.summary: Rank a competitive page by surrounding it with a complete ecosystem of related content on the topic, rather than publishing one isolated page.
cards.use_when: Planning the content roadmap that supports a key category page, product page or service page.
